title: Counit normalization of the finite identity-point dualizing object
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $B=A_s$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].
Let $G=A_{s,\mathrm{et}}$ and $
u:s_{\mathrm{proet}}	o s_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Use the finite exceptional-inverse-image construction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] at $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$, with the identity compactification and the identity right adjoint of ordinary etale identity compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Then $A$ is finite, $B=
u^*G$ under the constant-ring comparison, and the identity dualizing object has the specified presentation $\omega=Ra_s^!B=
u^*R
u_*B$. If $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ are the unit and counit of $
u^*\dashv R
u_*$, the morphism $\alpha=\epsilon_B:\omega	o B$ is an isomorphism with inverse $
u^*(\eta_G)$. These equalities are in the derived category and use the constant-ring identification; in particular the normalization is the actual comparison counit.

source.place: Opening sentence: identity compact support and its right adjoint; finite comparison counit normalization (old item step 1).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value], the absolute value on $E$ is nonarchimedean. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], its valuation ring $R$ is a DVR with finite residue field and maximal ideal $\varpi R$. Apply [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], clause (2), with $K=E$, $\mathcal O=R$ and the chosen $\varpi$: since $n\ge1$, $A=R/\varpi^nR$ is finite. This is the coefficient ring of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].

source.place: Finite coefficient datum in the opening sentence; finiteness supplied by the existing valued-DVR quotient lemma.

proof.text: The comparison is a geometric morphism by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Apply [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] to it with $\Lambda=A$. Its canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $\nu^{-1}A_{s,\mathrm{et}}\cong A_s$ preserves the scalar sections. On the regular rank-one module this is also the module comparison, hence $\nu^*G=B$. Exactness in the same lemma gives this identification for these degree-zero objects in the bounded-below derived category.

proof.text:
For the identity compactification, [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $R(\operatorname{id})_*\operatorname{id}_!$. Extension and direct image along the identity act as the identity on complexes and maps, so $D\operatorname{id}_!=\operatorname{id}$, and $R(\operatorname{id})_*Q L=Q I$ for a K-injective resolution $L	o I$; the image $Q(L	o I)$ of this resolution is an isomorphism, natural in $L$, so the compact-support functor is naturally isomorphic to the identity, not literally equal to it. Hence the identity functor is a right adjoint of it, with the adjunction transported along this isomorphism; this is the identity right adjoint stipulated in the statement, and the right adjoint $f^	imes$ in the finite formula is only determined up to unique isomorphism, so this choice is permitted. Substitution in the finite formula $Rf_n^!=
u_X^*f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] gives $\omega=
u^*R
u_*B$.

proof.text:
The comparison theorem is stated for modules over the coefficient ring sheaf $(U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),A))^\#$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], whereas $B$ is a module over the constant ring sheaf $A_s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison] with $\mathcal O_E=R$, the chosen $\varpi$, $T=s$ and level $n$: its isomorphisms $\kappa_n$ and $e_n$ identify this ring sheaf with the constant ring sheaf of $A$, carrying each constant scalar to the same constant, and restriction of scalars along them is an exact equivalence of module categories. Both inverse images are defined by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] on underlying sheaves and the scalar endomorphisms $\lambda_r$, so this equivalence identifies $D^+$, $
u^*$, $R
u_*$ and the adjunction used below with those of the theorem. The object $G=A_{s,\mathrm{et}}[0]$ is bounded below and $A$ is finite by step 1, so [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] makes $\eta_G:G	o R
u_*
u^*G$ invertible. Put $ eta=
u^*(\eta_G):B	o\omega$, using steps 2 and 3. Its inverse is $
u^*(\eta_G^{-1})$, by functoriality. The left triangle identity for the given adjunction says $\epsilon_{
u^*G}\circ
u^*(\eta_G)=1_{
u^*G}$. Under the constant-ring identification of step 2 and naturality of $\epsilon$ this is $\epsilon_B\circ eta=1_B$. Composing on the right with $ eta^{-1}$ gives $\epsilon_B= eta^{-1}$, so also $ eta\circ\epsilon_B=1_\omega$. Thus the actual counit $\alpha=\epsilon_B$ is an isomorphism with the asserted inverse.
